findings.title: getClientsWithPermission includes the "Clients" all-resource name in result set
findings.body: resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) iterates over every resource of type "Clients", which includes both per-client resources (named client.getId()) and the all-clients resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() with the name "Clients". When the caller holds an all-clients scope permission, hasGrantedPermission returns true for that all-clients resource and the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set alongside any real client UUIDs. Callers using this set to filter or load clients will misinterpret the resource-type string as a client ID (lookups will fail) and the absence of a distinct "all" indicator means the all-clients case is silently lost. The loop must either skip the all-clients resource (compare resource.getName() to AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) or model the all-clients case as a separate sentinel.

findings.title: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) can NPE when all-clients resource is missing
findings.body: When no per-client resource exists, the code loads the all-clients resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). If the schema resource server has not been initialized (or the resource was otherwise removed), getResourceTypeResource returns null, and the subsequent authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) is invoked with a null resource and throws a NullPointerException. This path is reached on every per-client permission check when no all-clients policy has been created yet, so it is reachable in production during early realm setup. Add a null check on the resource returned from getResourceTypeResource before calling findByResource.

findings.title: registerListener gates V2-only deployments off event-driven cleanup
findings.body: The new wrapper uses Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (the legacy V1 flag), but the listener body delegates to management(...) which dispatches on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 and can return MgmtPermissionsV2. When a realm runs with only V2 enabled and V1 disabled, the entire listener body is now skipped, so ClientRemovedEvent, RoleRemovedEvent, and GroupRemovedEvent will not trigger any cleanup of the V2 resources/scopes/policies those objects back. The check needs to consider ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (either in addition to or instead of the V1 flag) so that pure-V2 realms still receive the event-driven cleanup.

findings.title: Javadocs on several interface methods omit V2 behavior notes
findings.body: Methods such as canList(), requireList(), canViewClientScopes(), requireViewClientScopes(), canListClientScopes(), requireListClientScopes(), and requireView() are newly documented in this PR but, unlike canManage/canView/canView(ClientModel)/canConfigure(ClientModel)/canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles, do not include the "For V2 only: ..." clause that explains the FGAP fallback used by ClientPermissionsV2. Because ClientPermissionsV2 does not override any of these (canList/canViewClientScopes/canListClientScopes all fall through to the V1 implementation), readers cannot tell how these methods behave under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Add the missing "For V2 only" notes (or note explicitly that they inherit V1 behavior unchanged) so the contract is clear.

findings.title: No integration test for VIEW-per-client or all-clients CONFIGURE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE in V2
findings.body: PermissionClientTest adds coverage for MANAGE per-client (testManageOnlyOneClient), CONFIGURE per-client (testConfigureOnlyOneClient), MANAGE all-clients (testManageAllClients), VIEW all-clients (testViewAllClients), and MAP_ROLES+MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE per-client (testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient). It never exercises VIEW scoped to a single client, CONFIGURE granted on the all-clients resource, or MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE at all. Since ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel), canConfigure(ClientModel) (all-clients branch in hasPermission) and canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) are brand new code paths, at least one positive and one negative test for each is needed to lock in behavior; without them, regressions in those branches (for example the "Clients" leak in getClientsWithPermission, or the NPE in hasPermission) will not be caught.
